question: Enteric-coated tablets should never be crushed or chewed, because crushing destroys the protective coat and exposes the drug to gastric acid, leading to drug inactivation or gastric irritation.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: Enteric coatings are pH-sensitive polymer films. They resist stomach acid (pH 1–3) and dissolve at intestinal pH (>6). Crushing an enteric-coated tablet exposes the drug directly to gastric acid.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. Enteric coating is specifically designed to resist gastric pH and dissolve only in the alkaline intestinal environment. Crushing it defeats this purpose entirely.
